note: Made-up history of a small bakery. Every name, price, key and date here is invented. It is the only history in this repository.

messages.text: I want to make delivery free for bigger orders. Most baskets are around $30. What threshold makes sense?
With baskets around $30, a threshold a little above that nudges people to add one more item. $40 is a common choice: it is reachable with one extra loaf and a pastry.
let's make delivery free over $40.
Done. Free delivery now applies to orders over $40. Orders under that keep the $6 delivery fee.
Dunmore Grain just told me their bread flour is going up 18 percent from February. I can't absorb that.

An 18 percent rise on your main ingredient is large. Two mills nearby sell comparable strong white flour: Hartwell Mills and Pennybrook. Hartwell quotes per 12.5 kg bag and delivers monthly; Pennybrook delivers weekly but has a higher minimum.
Monthly is fine, we have the dry store. Go with Hartwell Mills. Forty bags, delivered the first Monday of each month.

Set. Hartwell Mills, forty 12.5 kg bags of strong white flour, delivered on the first Monday of each month, paid by transfer within fourteen days. I have drafted the notice to Dunmore Grain ending the standing order.
Send it.
Sent. The last Dunmore delivery is January 27.
Write down our hours properly. Weekdays we open at 7.
Noted. Weekday opening is 7 am. What about the weekend?
Saturday 8 am, closed Sunday. We close at 3 every open day.
Recorded: Monday to Friday 7 am to 3 pm, Saturday 8 am to 3 pm, closed Sunday.
The order form on the site is letting people order for tomorrow at 4 pm. The cutoff is supposed to be 2 pm.
I looked at the form's cutoff check. It compares against the server's clock, which is set to UTC, so 2 pm on the server is the middle of the night for you.
Here is the payment test key in case you need to run a test order: sk_test_MADEUP51Hq9crumbkettle0000
Thanks. I set the form's timezone to Pacific/Auckland and ran three test orders: 1:55 pm is accepted for tomorrow, 2:05 pm is offered the day after, and midnight behaves correctly.
Good. Ship it.
Shipped. The next-day cutoff is 2 pm Pacific/Auckland time, and the form now shows the cutoff under the date picker.
I keep forgetting the starter. Help me fix a schedule for Gerald.
Gerald the starter does best on a steady rhythm. How warm is the kitchen overnight?
About 24 degrees by the ovens. Feed at 6 am and 6 pm?
That works. Feed Gerald at 6 am and 6 pm. At 24 degrees, plan the bulk ferment for five hours, with a fold every hour for the first three.
Five hours at 24 degrees, got it.
Written on the kitchen sheet: feeds at 6 am and 6 pm, bulk ferment five hours at 24 degrees.
Van fuel is killing the margin on small deliveries. raise the free delivery threshold to $60 from Monday.
Updated. From Monday March 9, free delivery starts at $60. Orders under $60 keep the $6 fee. I changed the banner on the site and the note on the printed menu file.
Thanks.
You're welcome. I will check order sizes after two weeks and tell you whether baskets moved.
Roster. Priya opens Tuesday to Thursday. Tom does both weekend days, but we only open Saturday so that's one day.
Recorded: Priya opens Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. Tom works Saturday. Who covers the Saturday counter while Tom bakes?
Nobody yet. I need a Saturday counter helper. Tom said his cousin might want it, he's asking her.
Open item: hire a Saturday counter helper. Waiting on Tom to hear back from his cousin.
Easter. Hot cross buns: what did we charge last year, and should we do a chocolate one?
Last year's price is not in anything I can see. For this year, ingredient cost per bun is about $1.30. A chocolate version would need its own allergen line and a separate tray rotation.
Then no chocolate version, I don't want a second allergen line in Easter week. $4.50 each, six for $24.
Set for Easter: hot cross buns $4.50 each or six for $24. No chocolate version this year, to avoid a second allergen line during the busiest week.
People are queueing outside on Saturdays before we open. Move Saturday opening to 7:30 starting this week.
Done. From Saturday April 18, Saturday opening is 7:30 am. Closing stays 3 pm. I updated the hours on the site and the door sign file.
Tell Tom.
Message drafted for Tom: Saturday start moves half an hour earlier, to 7:30 am, from April 18.
I want a weekly email to regulars. Mailbrook or Postwing?
Both handle a list your size. Mailbrook is cheaper under 500 subscribers but has no scheduled sends on its free plan. Postwing includes scheduling and a simple sign-up form.
Scheduling matters. Postwing. Here's the key: pw_live_MADEUP_7f3a9c2e41
Connected Postwing. I imported the 412 addresses from the loyalty sheet and added the sign-up form to the site footer.
Send it Thursdays at 4 pm, when people plan the weekend.
Scheduled: the newsletter goes out every Thursday at 4 pm through Postwing, to 412 subscribers today.
Tom's cousin said no in the end, but Mei from the market stall wants the Saturday counter job. I said yes.
Good news. What are the terms?
She starts May 9. $27 an hour, 7:15 to 3:15.
Recorded and closed: Mei is the Saturday counter helper from May 9, $27 an hour, 7:15 am to 3:15 pm. The open item about hiring a Saturday helper is done.
The deck oven is running 20 degrees hot on the left side.
That pattern usually points to the thermostat or its probe. Kessler Service looks after that oven brand locally.
They came this morning. Kessler replaced the thermostat. $380.
Recorded: Kessler Service replaced the deck oven thermostat on May 19 for $380. Is there a warranty on the part?
12 months. And from now on always give me prices including GST.
Understood. I will always give prices including GST. The thermostat carries a 12 month warranty, to May 2027.
Winter menu. Add the pumpkin scone. Take the lemon tart off until spring.
Done: pumpkin scone added, lemon tart off the menu until spring. Any change to coffee?
No, we stay with Ridgeback Roasters.
Coffee stays with Ridgeback Roasters. The winter menu file is updated and dated June 4.

nothing, just checking the new laptop works
It works. Enjoy the new laptop.
